papers.title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
papers.authors: Yimeng Lv, Jixia Huang, Shixiang Zong, Tong Yang, Chong Zhao
papers.abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. We specifically examined how needle-leaved forest landscape patterns interact with environmental conditions to shape the spread of PWD across regions. We applied the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) model to analyze the spatial differentiation of PWD outbreaks. Needle-leaved forest landscape metrics and environmental variables were integrated to evaluate their individual and combined effects on disease spread. PWD has progressively expanded over the past four decades. The epidemic was primarily distributed along the southeastern coastal zones and subsequently extended toward the northwestern interior. papers.title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
papers.authors: Deepak Subedi, Bharath Mallavarapu, Pranita Patil, Abhisek Niraula, Milan Kandel
papers.source: OpenAlex / Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
papers.abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. Preharvest interventions, including biosecurity, breeder and hatchery control, vaccination, litter and water management, feed hygiene, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, essential oils, bacteriophages, and bacteriocins, are evaluated according to mechanism, evidence strength, and commercial relevance. Postharvest interventions, including scalding, picking, evisceration control, chilling, peroxyacetic acid application, carcass rinses, post-chill treatments, and finished-product verification, are reviewed in relation to microbial reduction and process control. The review also discusses quantitative bio-mapping, surveillance design, whole-genome sequencing, predictive model

papers.title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Paddy Leaf Disease Detection Using an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 Model
papers.authors: B Johnson, Chandrakumar Thangavel
papers.abstract: The correct and prompt detection of leaf diseases in paddy crops remains essential for protecting agricultural output and yield stability and reducing major losses that occur during severe disease outbreaks. The widespread use of conventional centralized machine learning techniques becomes impractical for real-world agricultural applications, as their effectiveness diminishes under three main conditions: data privacy limitations, delayed transmission of information, along with reduced performance accuracy from non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data properties across different agro-climatic regions. This research develops a decentralized diagnostic system which combines Federated Learning with an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 model designed for paddy leaf disease classification. The Paddy Doctor dataset served as training material for the system which contained 16,225 RGB images that classified 12 disease types alongside healthy categories. The proposed model reached 98.7% classification accuracy and 98.5% precision and 98.6% F1-score while maintaining a final loss of 0.21 after 100 communication rounds. papers.title: A Survey of Object Detection and Classification in Video Using Deep Learning Approaches
papers.authors: Umar BELLO
papers.source: OpenAlex / INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
papers.abstract: Object detection and classification in videos has emerged as a core challenge in computer vision, with applications spanning autonomous driving, surveillance, healthcare, robotics, and human– computer interaction. Unlike still-image object detection, video-based detection requires handling additional complexities such as temporal coherence, motion blur, occlusion, and real-time constraints. Traditional approaches relying on handcrafted features and background subtraction have given way to deep learning-based methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), transformers, and one-stage detectors such as the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family. This paper provides a comprehensive review of object detection in videos, surveying the evolution of methods from early handcrafted approaches to recent deep architectures. We examine popular models, datasets, and benchmarks, with an emphasis on accuracy–speed trade-offs and the unique challenges of real-world deployment. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Multi-source temporal fusion and multi-station learning for early warning of diamondback moth infestation in Brassica crops
papers.authors: Dong Zhang, Jiale Wang
papers.abstract: Introduction Meteorological variability influences diamondback moth (DBM; Plutella xylostella ) infestation and the resulting damage to Brassica crops. Accurate multi-horizon forecasting requires models that preserve short-lived meteorological exposures while integrating thermal timing, spatial dependence, and recent infestation dynamics within a transparent framework. Methods The Temporal–Geospatial Pest Network (TG-PestNet) forecasts the weekly percentage of inspected plants classified as DBM-infested 1 to 4 weeks ahead at four Guangdong stations, from origin-time information only. It preserves hourly exposure, encodes lookback weeks on a thermal-time axis, couples stations through a wind-informed graph, and protects infestation history in a gated anchor. Evaluation used 344 synchronized weeks, 66 later test origins, 13 history-only comparators, retraining ablations, matched-width controls, and input-matched generic encoders. Results and discussion TG-PestNet achieved the lowest observed root-mean-square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error in all 12 station–metric combinations, with mean reductions of 5.9%–13.0%. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.title: Smart water management in agriculture: convergence of sensors, imaging, AI, precision irrigation, and robotics systems
papers.authors: Sachin Ghanghas, Naveen Sihag, Parveen Dhanger
papers.abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. Conventional water management systems often rely on uniform application, fixed scheduling, and limited real-time information, which overlooks spatial and temporal variation in soil, crop, and weather conditions and can result in water loss, over-irrigation, and under-irrigation. This review highlights studies on the integration of AI-driven sensing and imaging technologies, IoT-based precision irrigation, variable-rate technologies, digital twins, and agricultural robotics for crop water management. These approaches integrate field, crop, weather, and spatial information to support water-demand assessment, crop-stress monitoring, irrigation scheduling, site-specific application, and automated water management. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. papers.authors: Yumeng Liu, Gang Luo
papers.abstract: Background This research aimed to identify novel oxidative stress (OS)–related biomarkers and develop predictive models for the early detection of pediatric sepsis. Methods Five open-access datasets from the gene expression omnibus database were analyzed, which included peripheral whole blood samples from children with sepsis and healthy controls. Using bioinformatics approaches, we identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with OS. We then combined weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and multiple machine learning algorithms (ML) to identify seven candidate genes, constructed a protein–protein interaction (PPI) network to screen six hub genes, and evaluated their correlations with the immune microenvironment. We subsequently evaluated the diagnostic performance of the hub genes using training datasets (GSE26440 and GSE26378) and validation datasets (GSE13904, GSE8121, and GSE9692). Moreover, molecular docking analysis revealed interactions between hub gene–encoded proteins and small-molecule compounds, which helps predict drug sensitivity. papers.authors: Berta Pozzi, Agustina Magalí Lucero, Valeria Buggiano, Miguel Angel Pelaez, Cybele Garcia
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing is a key regulatory mechanism known to be altered upon viral infection. These alterations can arise both from direct viral interference with the splicing machinery and from cellular responses such as activation of innate immunity. Here, we investigated splicing changes shared between dengue virus (DENV) infection and interferon (IFN) treatment in cultured cells, the latter serving as a model for virus-independent innate immune activation. Among the common events, we identified an increased production of non-coding mRNA isoforms from the CLK1 gene, which gives rise to a kinase that phosphorylates splicing factors including SR proteins and spliceosomal components. Consistent with this finding, IFN treatment led to a reduction in CLK1 protein levels. Using stable cell lines with CRISPR/dCas9-mediated modulation of CLK1 expression, we found that silencing CLK1 enhanced the induction of immune response genes, while its over-expression attenuated it. Inhibition of CLK1 kinase activity with the pharmacological inhibitor TG003 further potentiated IFN-induced gene expression and reduced DENV replication. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.title: Land carbon sinks in the European Union are not keeping pace with carbon neutrality expectations
papers.authors: Behrouz Gholamahmadi, Eva Ivits
papers.abstract: Abstract The European Union has substantially reduced greenhouse-gas emissions since 1990, yet the land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sink has not strengthened in parallel. The EU-27 LULUCF balance was approximately −231 MtCO₂e in 2024, while the latest Member State projections indicate a remaining gap of 40–55 MtCO₂e to the binding −310 MtCO₂e target for 2030. Here, we synthesise recent assessments to examine the drivers of this weakening in the land carbon sink and their implications for the effectiveness of climate mitigation policy. Declining forest growth, increased harvesting, climate-driven disturbances, and rising biomass demand reduce net carbon uptake, with one 2040 GLOBIOM sensitivity analysis indicating an approximately 100 MtCO₂e reduction in the LULUCF sink under an additional 20 Mtoe of woody-biomass demand. Concurrently, the EU inventory reported 52.7% uncertainty in the 2022 LULUCF level and 29.4% uncertainty in its trend, while important soil-carbon dynamics remain incompletely represented. papers.authors: Alfredo Morales-León, Maritza Peñaflor-Ramírez, Citlalli Mejia-Garza, Isela Jasso-Flores, Alejandra Miranda-Carrazco
papers.abstract: Abstract Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, yet their biodiversity remains understudied compared to humid tropical forests. We integrated functional trait ecology with environmental vulnerability assessments to evaluate multi‑causal disturbances affecting amphibians and reptiles in Oaxaca, Mexico, a hotspot of endemism and biodiversity loss. Environmental Vulnerability Scores (EVS) were constructed for the complete herpetofaunal assemblage and compared against international (IUCN) and national (NOM‑059) classifications. Significant discrepancies emerged: reptiles (n = 222) exhibited higher EVS than amphibians (n = 99), yet 14% of reptile species and 2% of amphibian species remain Data Deficient or Not Evaluated by the IUCN. NOM‑059 assessments were more limited, with nearly half of species Not Listed. Trait‑based analyses revealed that landscape transformation drives species‑specific vulnerability. Amphibians were disproportionately affected due to endemicity, low abundance, and sensitivity to environmental change, compounded by pollution and disease. papers.title: Curvularia lunata as a versatile pathogen causing leaf spot diseases in diverse plant species and its management strategies
papers.authors: M. Qaisar, Muhammad Sarmad Atiq, Abdul Mubeen Lodhi, Azeem Akram, Muhammad Usman
papers.abstract: Curvularia lunata poses a significant threat to agricultural ecosystems worldwide, causing substantial yield losses and economic consequences across a variety of crops. As a prominent phytopathogenic fungus known for its affinity for leaf spot diseases, its proliferation warrants attention due to its remarkable adaptability and expanding influence. It can serve as a beneficial endophyte for certain plants; however, its pathogenic nature underscores its potential to affect both plant and human health. This review explores key characteristics of C. lunata , including its morphology characterized by dark, velvety colonies and distinctive crescent-shaped spores. Its ecological role as a plant pathogen is examined, emphasizing the damage it can inflict on crops. Additionally, C. lunata is known to produce various secondary metabolites, including phytotoxic and other biologically active compounds. papers.title: Treating a systemic disease as a local one: failure points of current pancreatic cancer management and a multimodal, biology-guided framework for redesign
papers.authors: Patrick E. Sewell
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the most lethal solid tumors, with 5-year survival near 13% despite decades of incremental change, and current management continues to be organized around anatomic resectability and a chemotherapy backbone applied largely without regard to tumor biology. papers.title: Integrated strategies for improving lodging resistance in wheat: physiological mechanisms, plant growth regulators and agronomic management
papers.authors: Kavita Devi, Jasdev Singh Deol, Amit Kaul, Arun Kumar, Rahul Sharma
papers.abstract: Wheat lodging remains a major constraint to sustainable wheat production because it reduces grain yield and quality, increases harvesting losses and lowers production efficiency. The widespread cultivation of high-yielding cultivars, intensive nitrogen fertilization, higher planting densities, expansion of irrigated agriculture, and increasingly frequent extreme weather events have collectively increased lodging susceptibility, making effective management an important priority. Lodging is a complex phenomenon governed by interactions among plant architecture, stem mechanical properties, root anchorage, crop management practices and environmental conditions. Consequently, improving lodging resistance requires an integrated approach that combines physiological understanding with practical agronomic interventions. This review synthesizes recent advances in the structural, physiological, biochemical and agronomic mechanisms underlying lodging resistance in wheat. papers.authors: Barbara Piškur, Ana Brglez, M. Žerjav, Maarten De Groot, ̧Nikica Ogris
papers.abstract: Biovarnost v pridelavi sadik gozdnega drevja vpliva na uspešnost obnove gozdov s sadnjo in setvijo in na dolgoročno odpornost gozdnih ekosistemov, zlasti v razmerah podnebnih sprememb in globalizacije. Čeprav so drevesnice prepoznane kot okolje pojavljanja bolezni in škodljivcev, njihov pomen kot vstopne točke biotskih tveganj v gozdni prostor v praksi ostaja podcenjen. Prispevek izpostavlja glavne skupine biotskih dejavnikov tveganja, ki se lahko v drevesnicah pojavljajo latentno in se s sadilnim materialom prenesejo na obnovitvena rastišča. Na podlagi pregleda literature in podatkov iz slovenskega prostora obravnavamo tveganja prenosa škodljivih organizmov iz drevesnic v gozdne in sorodne ekosisteme ter ključne značilnosti slovenskega sistema pridelave sadik z vidika biovarnosti. Posebna pozornost je namenjena sistemskim značilnostim, kot so centralizacija pridelave, mešana struktura drevesnic in omejitve obstoječih nadzornih mehanizmov. V zaključku so podane usmeritve za krepitev biovarnosti, ki temeljijo na preventivnem upravljanju tveganj, nadzoru vhodnih materialov, spremljanju zdravstvenega stanja sadik ter vključevanju biovarnostnih meril v programe in prakse pridelave sadi

papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. This reframes a persistent gap in philosophy of mind: qualia have long been debated while the physical architecture that must bound it has been neglected. papers.title: Interconnected communication mechanisms in plants and their ecological functions and agricultural implications
papers.authors: Shah Mohammad Naimul Islam, Nuril Huda, Meem Afrose Oaishi, Md. Abul Kalam Azad, Razia Sultana
papers.abstract: Plants interact through a coordinated communication network that enables them to perceive, process, and respond to environmental stimuli. This communication network consists of complex biological systems, including root systems, volatile organic compounds, RNA-based molecular signals, and fungal networks. Plants use these interconnected pathways to share information that regulates defense activation, resource distribution, and developmental processes. This review discusses the mechanisms of plant communication, the impacts of climate change on interplant signaling, and their ecological and agricultural significance. These insights will advance our understanding of plant survival strategies, community dynamics, and crop productivity within the broader context of ecology and sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Same Problem, Different Field: Cross-Domain Solution Import via Domain-Stripped Computational Fingerprints
papers.authors: Eryk Kulikowski
papers.source: OpenAlex / ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: The same underlying computational problem is solved across unrelated fields under different names: recursive Bayesian state estimation appears as a “Kalman filter” in control, “Bayesian forecasting” in pharmacokinetics, and “data assimilation” in geoscience. Topical and citation-based scientific embeddings cannot see this shared problem. We distill each paper once into a domain- and method-name-stripped faceted computational fingerprint, a free-text mechanism skeleton plus controlled computational facets. We define a tunable, facet-selectable similarity over it. The goal is solution import: surface cross-field pairs solving the same problem, so a bespoke implementation can be swapped for another field’s standard, specialized solver. On a benchmark of 18 method families across 109 papers, the skeleton lifts cross-domain retrieval average precision over the abstract from 0.222 to 0.513, and the whole fingerprint reaches 0.557. Strikingly, four trained scientific embedders all fall below plain abstract+TF-IDF: they encode topical and citation similarity, the wrong signal for this task. Methods This study profiled alterations in the virome and microbiome in 143 SARS-CoV-2–positive adults, stratified by disease severity (Non-Severe, Severe, Critical), compared with 96 RT-PCR–negative controls.
